text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "send_sms(phone: str, text: str, *, now=None) -> dict sends one text: it checks feature('sms_enabled') (raises RuntimeError if disabled), enforces len(text) <= MAX_LENGTH (160, raises ValueError), then appends a record {\"id\", \"phone\", \"text\", \"queued_at\"} to data/outbox/sms.jsonl and returns it. The id is format_sms_id(next_number([m['id'] for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')). Note: send_sms does NOT accept or write household_id/template_id/params fields, so a resend that must carry the same details as the original cannot get them through send_sms's record as-is.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "The outbox is append-only and irreversible: 'send_sms() appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl, and the SMS gateway sends every line in that file. Nothing ever removes or edits a line in the outbox.' A line in the outbox counts as SENT. store has deliberately no function to edit or delete a line in an append-only file.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "delivery_status() -> dict[str, str] reads data/sms_status.json (returns {} if the file doesn't exist), mapping SMS id to 'delivered' or 'failed'. New messages have no entry yet. sent_messages() -> list[dict] reads data/outbox/sms.jsonl via store.read_jsonl.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "Current gateway status data: SMS-00001, SMS-00004, SMS-00005, SMS-00006, SMS-00009, SMS-00010, SMS-00012, SMS-00018, SMS-00019, SMS-00020 are 'failed' (10 messages); SMS-00002, 03, 07, 08, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 are 'delivered'.", "file": "data/sms_status.json"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "Each existing outbox line has the shape {\"id\": \"SMS-NNNNN\", \"household_id\": \"HH-NNNNC\", \"phone\": \"+999 NNNNNNNN\", \"template_id\": \"DELIVERY_DAY\", \"params\": {\"site\": ..., \"day\": ...}, \"text\": ..., \"queued_at\": \"2026-02-25T12:00:00\"}. A resend with 'the same message and details as the original' should reuse the original's phone, text, household_id, template_id and params, with a new SMS id and new queued_at.", "file": "data/outbox/sms.jsonl"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "ID helpers: format_sms_id(number: int) -> 'SMS-{number:05d}' and next_number(existing_ids, prefix: str) -> int returns 1 + the highest number used with that prefix (max(numbers, default=0) + 1). SMS ids are SMS-NNNNN per core/ids.py docstring.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "store helpers: store.read_jsonl(name) -> list[dict] (empty list if file missing), store.append_jsonl(name, record) appends one JSON line, store.read_json(name), store.write_json(name, obj) (atomic via tmp + os.replace), store.path(name) -> Path under data_dir(). data_dir() is LIFELINE_DATA_DIR env var or repo data/.", "file": "core/store.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "Ops scripts live in scripts/ and are run from the Lifeline root (scripts/stock_report.py does sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)) then imports). 'Scripts that send payments or SMS, or change data/registry.json or data/ledger.json, must say so in their docstring.'", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "config.settings: feature('sms_enabled') is True; now() returns datetime.fromisoformat(LIFELINE_NOW env or '2026-03-10T08:00:00'); send_sms uses (now or _now()).isoformat(timespec='seconds') for queued_at.", "file": "config/settings.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "data/audit.jsonl is append-only audit log; existing entries are {\"event\": \"payment\", \"actor\": \"scripts/cycle_payments.py\", \"ref\": ..., \"at\": ...}. No SMS audit entries exist yet; a resend script may follow this pattern (event/actor/ref/at) if it audits.", "file": "data/audit.jsonl"}]}}
reasoning: I have enough. Note: outbox records include household_id, template_id, params — send_sms() only takes phone/text and doesn't include those fields. The resend script should preserve household_id/template_id/params. send_sms signature: send_sms(phone, text, *, now=None) — appends with id, phone, text, queued_at only. So the script may need to append records with extra fields, or use send_sms and lose household_id. Worth reporting. Also audit.jsonl is append-only; scripts that send SMS must say so in docstring.
